en: be arranged in a row; be listed

examples.ko: 책상 위에 연필이 길게 나열되어 있어요.
examples.en: Pencils are lined up in a long row on the desk.
The names are listed in alphabetical order.
The names of dishes were listed one after another on the menu.

examples.ko: 보고서에서 문제점이 순서대로 나열된 부분을 읽었어요.
examples.en: I read the part of the report where the problems are listed in order.
I wipe the things that will be lined up on the shelf first.

examples.ko: 이유가 너무 많이 나열되면 말이 길어져요.
examples.en: If too many reasons are listed, the talk gets long.

explain: '나열하다'는 사람이 늘어놓는 것이고, '나열되다'는 늘어놓아진 상태를 말해요. '쭉', '순서대로' 같은 말과 자주 써요. 목록이나 항목이 이어질 때 글에서 많이 나와요.
explain_en: '나열하다' is what a person does; '나열되다' describes things that end up laid out in a row. It often goes with '쭉' or '순서대로', and shows up mostly in writing when items follow one another in a list.

examples.en: When I read a book, I get completely absorbed.
He got so absorbed in the game that he forgot to eat.

examples.ko: 일에 몰입하는 사람은 시간이 빨리 가요.
examples.en: For people absorbed in their work, time goes fast.
Please turn off your phone so you can get into the movie.
The child was absorbed in drawing.

examples.ko: 몰입할 수 있는 취미가 있으면 좋아요.
examples.en: It is nice to have a hobby you can lose yourself in.

explain: 보통 '~에 몰입하다'로 써요. '집중하다'는 눈앞의 일에 주의를 모으는 것이고, '몰입하다'는 시간이 가는 줄 모를 만큼 깊이 빠지는 느낌이에요. '빠지다'보다 격식 있는 말이에요.
explain_en: It is usually used as '~에 몰입하다'. '집중하다' means gathering your attention on what is in front of you; '몰입하다' means being so deep in it that you lose track of time. It is a bit more formal than '빠지다'.

en: defend to the death; hold on to at all costs

examples.en: The soldiers defended this bridge to the very end.

examples.ko: 우리 팀은 1위 자리를 사수하려고 열심히 뛰어요.
examples.en: Our team plays hard to hold on to first place.
It was cool to see the players guarding the goal at all costs.

examples.ko: 마을 사람들은 오래된 나무를 사수하기로 했어요.
examples.en: The villagers decided to protect the old tree at all costs.
I came out determined to hold on to this spot.

examples.ko: 반드시 사수해야 할 곳이라서 군인이 많이 있어요.
examples.en: It is a place that must be held, so there are many soldiers.

explain: 싸움이나 경기에서 '지키다'를 아주 강하게 말할 때 써요. 목숨을 걸 만큼 센 느낌이라 뉴스나 스포츠 기사에 자주 나와요. 일상 대화에서는 '지키다'를 더 많이 써요.
explain_en: A very strong version of '지키다' used in fights and matches, with the feel of defending something at any cost. It is common in news and sports reports; in everyday talk people simply say '지키다'.

en: come to an end; be ended; be concluded

examples.en: The meeting wrapped up in an hour.
The long trial has finally come to an end.
When the case is closed, I will let you know the result.
I did not know it would end like this.
Please check the date when the lawsuit is concluded.

examples.ko: 싸움이 종결된 뒤에 모두 집으로 돌아갔어요.
examples.en: After the fight was over, everyone went home.

explain: '끝나다'와 같은 뜻이지만 딱딱해서 뉴스나 서류에 자주 나와요. 친구와 이야기할 때는 '끝나다'가 자연스러워요. 사람이 일부러 끝내면 '종결하다', 저절로 끝나면 '종결되다'를 써요.
explain_en: Same idea as '끝나다' but stiff, so it appears in news and documents; with friends '끝나다' sounds more natural. When someone ends it on purpose use '종결하다'; when it just ends, '종결되다'.

examples.en: The judge concluded the trial.

examples.ko: 회사는 이번 달에 조사를 종결할 거예요.
examples.en: The company will wrap up the investigation this month.
We decided to end the discussion here.
The CEO closed the meeting and stood up.
I want to put an end to the old argument.
To settle the matter, you both have to apologize.

explain: '끝내다'의 딱딱한 말이에요. 회의·재판·조사처럼 공식적인 일에 주로 써요. 사람이 일부러 끝내면 '종결하다', 저절로 끝나면 '종결되다'예요.
explain_en: The stiff version of '끝내다', used mostly for formal things like meetings, trials and investigations. A person ending it on purpose is '종결하다'; something ending by itself is '종결되다'.

examples.en: My father rose to lieutenant colonel in the army.
The lieutenant colonel gave a greeting in front of the unit.
That lieutenant colonel is kind to his men.
My uncle will soon be promoted to lieutenant colonel.

examples.ko: 영화에서 중령 역할을 맡은 배우가 멋있었어요.
examples.en: The actor who played the lieutenant colonel in the movie was cool.
Above lieutenant colonel there is colonel.

explain: 군대 계급이에요. 소령 위, 대령 아래예요. 부를 때는 이름이나 계급 뒤에 '님'을 붙여 '중령님'이라고 해요.
explain_en: A military rank, above 소령 (major) and below 대령 (colonel). When addressing the person, add '님' and say '중령님'.

examples.en: Fatigue builds up in the body.
When long experience accumulates, your skill grows.
Knowledge does not accumulate overnight.
The more data accumulates, the more accurate the results get.
Heat has built up in the room, so it is hot.

examples.ko: 이 기술은 수십 년 동안 축적된 노력의 결과예요.
examples.en: This technology is the result of effort accumulated over decades.

explain: '쌓이다'보다 딱딱한 말로, 경험·지식·자료·피로처럼 눈에 안 보이는 것에 자주 써요. 먼지나 눈처럼 눈에 보이는 것은 '쌓이다'가 더 자연스러워요. 사람이 모으는 쪽은 '축적하다'예요.
explain_en: A stiffer word than '쌓이다', often used for invisible things like experience, knowledge, data and fatigue. For visible things like dust or snow, '쌓이다' sounds more natural. The person-does-it form is '축적하다'.

examples.ko: 카페인을 과다하게 마시면 잠이 안 와요.
examples.en: If you drink too much caffeine, you cannot sleep.
Costs are excessive this month, so I am worried.

examples.ko: 정보가 과다한 시대에는 필요한 것만 골라야 해요.
examples.en: In an age of information overload, you have to pick only what you need.

examples.ko: 설탕이 과다한 음료는 몸에 안 좋아요.
examples.en: Drinks with too much sugar are bad for you.
The workload was excessive, so I worked until late at night.
Excessive greed actually ruins things.

explain: '너무 많다'를 공식적으로 말할 때 써요. 음식·비용·정보·업무처럼 양을 말하고, '과다하게', '과다한' 형태로 자주 나와요. 모자랄 때는 '부족하다'라고 해요.
explain_en: The formal way to say 'too much'. It is used for amounts of food, cost, information or work, usually as '과다하게' or '과다한'. When there is too little, say '부족하다'.

en: treat favorably; give preferential treatment to

examples.ko: 이 가게는 학생을 우대해서 값을 깎아 줘요.
examples.en: This shop gives students special treatment and a discount.
The company gives preference to people who are good at English.
The bank decided to give special treatment to long-time customers.

examples.ko: 외국어 능력자를 우대한다고 공고에 쓰여 있어요.
examples.en: The posting says people with language skills are preferred.
There is a discount program that favors seniors.

examples.ko: 회사가 경력자를 우대해 줘서 월급을 더 받았어요.
examples.en: The company gave preference to experienced workers, so I got a higher salary.

explain: 채용 공고의 '영어 가능자 우대'처럼 명사로도 자주 보여요. '우대하다'는 더 좋은 조건을 주는 쪽이 주어이고, 받는 쪽은 '우대받다'를 써요. 반대로 홀대하는 말은 '푸대접하다'예요.
explain_en: In job postings you often see it as a noun, as in '영어 가능자 우대' (English speakers preferred). The side giving the better terms is the subject of '우대하다', and the side receiving them uses '우대받다'. The opposite, treating someone coldly, is '푸대접하다'.

examples.ko: 그 사람이 원망스러워서 말도 하기 싫어요.
examples.en: I resent him so much that I do not even want to talk.

examples.ko: 시험에 떨어지니 공부 안 한 내가 원망스러웠어요.
examples.en: After failing the test, I blamed myself for not studying.

examples.ko: 약속을 어긴 친구가 원망스럽지만 이해도 돼요.
examples.en: I resent my friend who broke the promise, but I understand too.
He looked at me with reproachful eyes.

examples.ko: 비가 와서 소풍을 못 가니 날씨가 원망스러워요.
examples.en: We cannot go on the picnic because of rain, so I resent the weather.
Nobody helped me, so I felt bitter toward the world.

explain: 기대했는데 서운해서 탓하고 싶은 마음이에요. 실망한 느낌이 들어 있어요. 사람이 아닌 날씨나 세상에도 쓸 수 있어요. 탓하는 행동은 동사 '원망하다'예요.
explain_en: The feeling of wanting to blame someone because you hoped for more and were let down. It carries disappointment, and can be aimed at things like the weather or the world. The action of blaming is the verb '원망하다'.

examples.en: The police chased the thief to the end.

examples.ko: 우리 팀이 앞선 팀을 빠르게 추격하고 있어요.
examples.en: Our team is quickly closing in on the leading team.

examples.ko: 차를 타고 범인을 추격하는 장면이 나왔어요.
examples.en: There was a scene of chasing the criminal by car.
The runner chasing from behind turned it around at the end.
Do not chase a person running away; report it.

examples.ko: 누가 추격해 오는 것 같아서 무서웠어요.
examples.en: It felt like someone was coming after me, and I was scared.

explain: '쫓다', '쫓아가다'보다 딱딱하고 뉴스나 영화에 자주 나와요. 범인을 잡으려고 따라갈 때, 스포츠에서 앞선 팀을 따라잡으려 할 때 써요. 장난으로 따라갈 때는 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: Stiffer than '쫓다' or '쫓아가다' and common in news and films. Used when running after a criminal or when a team tries to catch up with the leader; not for playful chasing.

examples.ko: 독서는 상상력을 함양하는 데 도움이 돼요.
examples.en: Reading helps cultivate imagination.

examples.ko: 이 수업은 학생의 창의력을 함양하려고 만들었어요.
examples.en: This class was made to foster students' creativity.

examples.ko: 어릴 때부터 인성을 함양해야 한다고 생각해요.
examples.en: I think character should be cultivated from childhood.
I exercise every day to build up my stamina.

examples.ko: 시민 의식을 함양하기 위해 봉사 활동에 참여했어요.
examples.en: I joined volunteer work to cultivate a sense of civic responsibility.
Education is about cultivating the right values.

explain: 능력이나 마음가짐을 서서히 길러 줄 때 쓰는 책 같은 말이에요. '창의력/인성/체력/소양을 함양하다'처럼 짝이 정해져 있어요. 일상 대화에서는 '기르다'가 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: A bookish word for gradually developing an ability or attitude. It pairs with words like creativity, character, stamina and cultural literacy. In daily conversation '기르다' is more natural.

examples.ko: 경기가 끝날 때가 되자 분위기가 고조됐어요.
examples.en: As the game neared its end, the mood heightened.

examples.ko: 두 나라 사이의 긴장이 고조되고 있어요.
examples.en: Tension between the two countries is rising.
When the concert started, the excitement rose to the max.
The emotion swells as the song goes toward its second half.
Interest will rise as the election gets closer.

examples.ko: 갈등이 고조되기 전에 이야기를 해 봐요.
examples.en: Let's talk before the conflict escalates.

explain: 분위기·긴장·감정·관심처럼 눈에 안 보이는 것이 점점 높아질 때 써요. 기대나 흥분 같은 좋은 쪽에도, 긴장이나 갈등 같은 나쁜 쪽에도 써요. 온도나 값이 오를 때는 '오르다'를 써요.
explain_en: Used when something intangible like mood, tension, feeling or interest keeps rising. It fits both good things (excitement) and bad ones (tension, conflict). For temperature or prices going up, use '오르다'.

examples.en: The doctor anesthetized the patient before the surgery.

examples.ko: 치과에서는 이를 뽑기 전에 잇몸을 마취해요.
examples.en: At the dentist they numb the gums before pulling a tooth.

examples.ko: 마취하면 아프지 않지만 깨어난 뒤에 졸릴 수 있어요.
examples.en: You feel no pain under anesthesia, but you may be sleepy afterward.
The vet put the puppy under and began the surgery.
The nurse explained which area would be numbed.

examples.ko: 수술 전에 전신을 마취한다고 해서 조금 무서웠어요.
examples.en: They said they would put me under general anesthesia before the surgery, so I was a little scared.

explain: 병원에서 하는 말이에요. 의사가 하는 일이라서 '마취하다'를 쓰고, 몸 일부만 하면 '부분 마취', 전체면 '전신 마취'라고 해요. 마취 기운이 없어지는 것은 '마취가 풀리다'예요.
explain_en: A hospital word. The doctor is the subject of '마취하다'; partial is '부분 마취' and whole-body is '전신 마취'. When the effect wears off, say '마취가 풀리다'.

examples.ko: 그 병은 어른이 되어서 발병하는 경우가 많아요.
examples.en: That illness often appears in adulthood.
Colds break out at a high rate in winter.

examples.ko: 이 병이 처음 발병한 곳은 작은 마을이었어요.
examples.en: The place where this disease first broke out was a small village.
When stress is severe, gastritis easily develops.

examples.ko: 갑자기 발병하면 바로 병원에 가야 해요.
examples.en: If you suddenly fall ill, you should go to the hospital right away.

examples.ko: 가족 중에 발병한 사람이 있어서 검사를 받았어요.
examples.en: Someone in my family got sick, so I took a test.

explain: 병이 처음 나타날 때 쓰는 말이에요. 뉴스나 병원 설명에 자주 나오고, 일상에서는 '병에 걸리다'가 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: Used when a disease first appears. It is common in news and medical explanations; in everyday talk '병에 걸리다' is more natural.

examples.en: The news said the typhoon had weakened.
If you do not exercise, your muscles weaken.

examples.ko: 두 나라의 관계가 점점 약화되고 있어요.
examples.en: Relations between the two countries are gradually weakening.
After losing again and again, the team's confidence dropped.

examples.ko: 약을 오래 먹으면 효과가 약화될 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you take a medicine for a long time, its effect can weaken.

examples.ko: 법의 힘이 약화되면 규칙을 지키지 않는 사람이 늘어요.
examples.en: When the force of the law weakens, more people break the rules.

explain: 힘·효과·관계처럼 어떤 것이 점점 약해질 때 써요. 반대말은 '강화되다'예요. 몸이 약해질 때는 '약해지다'가 일상적이고, '약화되다'는 뉴스나 글에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: Used when power, effect or a relationship gradually becomes weaker. The opposite is '강화되다'. In daily talk about a body getting weak, '약해지다' is more usual; '약화되다' appears in news and writing.
